```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE          # illustrative: the GDAL-CLI and network paths below
```

vrtstack writes GDAL multidimensional VRTs: small XML documents that let a
collection of rasters be read as one array through any GDAL multidim reader,
with no data copied. There are three ways in, for three situations.

```{r setup}
library(vrtstack)
```

## 1. Stack 2D rasters along a new dimension

The original job: you have 2D rasters (COGs, GeoTIFFs) that are slices of one
variable, and you want them as a single 3D array. `gdal_mdim_stack()` builds the
new axis from scratch.

```{r from-scratch}
# soil layers by depth
gdal_mdim_stack(
  files = c("soil_0cm.tif", "soil_30cm.tif", "soil_100cm.tif"),
  dim_name = "depth",
  dim_values = c(0, 30, 100),
  dim_type = "VERTICAL",
  dim_direction = "DOWN",
  dim_unit = "cm",
  output = "soil.vrt"
)
```

Evenly spaced values are detected and stored compactly as
`<RegularlySpacedValues>` rather than a long value list; dimension values can be
pulled from file names with a one-group regex and parsed as dates; and
`http(s)://` sources are wrapped in `/vsicurl/` automatically.

```{r from-scratch-time}
# a daily time series, dates parsed from the file names
gdal_mdim_stack(
  files = list.files(pattern = "temp_\\d{8}\\.tif$"),
  dim_name = "time",
  dim_values = "(\\d{8})",
  parse_format = "%Y%m%d",
  dim_type = "TEMPORAL",
  time_origin = "1970-01-01",
  time_unit = "days",
  output = "temperature.vrt"
)
```

The convenience wrappers `vrt_time_stack()`, `vrt_depth_stack()` and
`vrt_regular_stack()` cover the common cases with shorter calls.

Each source carries a `<SourceSlab>` with an explicit `count`, so a read through
the VRT opens only the sources it covers rather than every file.

## 2. Extend an existing multidimensional recipe

Some sources are already multidimensional (NetCDF, Zarr, HDF5) and may hold
several arrays at once. For these, the fastest route is to take a small "first
few files" VRT as a recipe and flesh it out to the full file set, re-writing
only the concat dimension and the per-array source lists. Everything else -
coordinate arrays, slab geometry, per-array scale/offset/unit/attributes - is
carried through verbatim.

```{r template-extend}
# `template = TRUE` auto-generates the recipe from the first n files via
# `gdal mdim mosaic`, then extends it to the whole set.
vrtstack(
  files = all_files,              # e.g. thousands of daily NetCDFs
  concat = "(\\d{8})", parse_format = "%Y%m%d",
  origin = "1978-01-01", unit = "days",
  template = TRUE, concat_dim = "time",
  output = "series.vrt"
)
```

The concat dimension need not be the first axis, nor named `"time"`: the axis
position is read from the recipe. A ready-made recipe can be passed instead of
`TRUE` (a path or an XML string).

`metadata_from` chooses which source donates the coordinate units and
root-group provenance restored onto an auto-generated recipe (`"first"`,
`"last"`, or an explicit path) - a repair for metadata that `gdal mdim mosaic`
drops. `graft_coord_units()` and `graft_group_attrs()` expose that repair
directly and are no-ops once the metadata is already present.

## 3. Emit a VRT from a catalog signature

When the grid is known from a catalog (STAC, CMR, or a URL template) rather than
by opening a file, the emitter path builds the VRT from two plain structures and
never touches the data: a *sources table* (one row per step) and a *signature*
(the grid and array metadata for the collection).

```{r emitter}
src <- mdim_sources(
  time = as.Date(c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-02")),
  dsn = c("/vsicurl/.../20240101.tif", "/vsicurl/.../20240102.tif"),
  source_ref = "1", kind = "band",          # a COG band; use "array" for NetCDF
  source_view = "[newaxis,...]"             # rank a 2D band up to the 3D cube
)

sig <- mdim_signature(
  collection = "demo", variable = "sst",
  nx = 1440, ny = 720,
  x0 = 0.125, dx = 0.25, y0 = 89.875, dy = -0.25,
  srs = "EPSG:4326", dtype = "Int16",
  nodata = -999, scale = 0.01, unit = "Celsius"
)

emit_mdim_vrt(src, sig, "demo.vrt")
```

The contract is "identical grid or refuse": the emitter trusts the signature, so
a collection whose assets are not on the same grid is a refusal, never a resample.
`stac_sufficiency()` reports whether a parsed STAC item carries the fields the
signature needs, and `verify_vrt()` round-trips an emitted VRT through
`gdal mdim info`.

## GDAL version note

The pure-XML paths - `gdal_mdim_stack()`, `mdim_template_extend()` and
`emit_mdim_vrt()` writing the document - work with any GDAL that gdalraster
links. The paths that drive GDAL's unified command-line algorithms through
`gdalraster::gdal_run()` - `verify_vrt()`, `template = TRUE` recipe generation,
and the metadata grafts - require **GDAL >= 3.11.3**.

## Reading the result

The VRT opens through any GDAL multidim reader: `gdalmdiminfo` and
`gdalmdimtranslate` on the command line, `gdalraster` in R, or an xarray GDAL
backend in Python. Selecting along the new dimension reads only the sources that
the selection covers.
